text:
elena-partnerships: Heads up — CloudVault procurement just rejected the MPA signing flow. They say their PO system requires a 'SignerAuthority' field in the PO XML and they will not accept DocuSign as the sole signature method. CC @alex-legal @ryan-ops

alex-legal: Do we have the rejection email or exact contract redline? What precisely are they asking for re: SSO?

elena-partnerships: Rejection email pasted in their note (redacted link): https://inboxes.example.com/cv/reject.
Quote: 'Cannot accept third-party signature; PO XML must include non-empty <SignerAuthority> and org_sso_claims.'

ryan-ops: We currently don't emit org_sso_claims in the marketplace PO webhook. Adding that would be a breaking change for other publishers. Can we negotiate a waiver or alternate metadata?

jiayi-se: Technical reality check: adding <SignerAuthority> and a couple of extra metadata nodes (OrgIdentifier, CertThumbprint) is feasible on the publisher side. The pipeline that converts portal orders -> our CP order webhook needs a small change. Rough ETA: 3–5 business days for dev + 1 day QA, assuming no schema churn.

matt-devrel: :thinking_face: CloudVault is on Azure marketplace. Historically some partners accepted a formal attestation + a signed letter from the vendor instead of embedding SSO claims. Worth asking if a signed attestation would unblock them while we implement schema changes.

alex-legal: I can draft an attestation letter. Before we do that, confirm exactly what metadata they require in the PO. If they insist on org_sso_claims, we should avoid embedding raw tokens — request only an immutable identifier + certificate thumbprint.

procurement-bot: Pulling latest marketplace PO spec... found azure_po_spec_v3.xml at /docs/marketplace/azure_po_spec_v3.xml

elena-partnerships: They included this example snippet in the rejection:
```xml
<PurchaseOrder>
  <POID>CV-12345</POID>
  <SignerAuthority/>
  <OrgIdentifier/>
</PurchaseOrder>
```
They explicitly require SignerAuthority to be non-empty and want either an SSO claim or a signed attestation attached to the PO.

ryan-ops: Short-term proposal: send a signed attestation + include a <SignerAuthority> element with the attestation reference. That avoids putting any SSO tokens in the PO. Needs legal sign-off.

alex-legal: I will draft the attestation language. We should offer two options to CloudVault: (1) accept the attestation + <SignerAuthority> node reference, or (2) accept an updated PO payload with <OrgIdentifier> and <CertThumbprint> (no live tokens). We should not send SSO tokens.

jiayi-se: Implementation approach for option (2): update the publisher lambda that generates PO XML to insert <SignerAuthority> and <OrgIdentifier> when the partner flags require it. Expose a feature flag per partner so others remain unchanged. Minimal risk.

matt-devrel: I'll reach out to the CloudVault AM now and propose the attestation path as interim. If they accept, engineering can ship the feature within 5 business days.

elena-partnerships: Pinged AM, copied legal. Waiting on response. If they refuse the attestation we escalate to marketplace partner manager to press for policy exception.

alex-legal: Draft complete, sending DM to elena. Note: if they forbid third-party signatures entirely (DocuSign), ask for a written procurement policy excerpt. We need that to make a formal escalation.

elena-partnerships: Will follow up when AM replies. Keeping thread updated. Thanks all.
